findings.title: ADR-004 recommends flock-based locking but text then contradicts itself by citing mkdir-based pattern
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md ADR-004 Consequences section (line 194) states: 'Mitigated by a flock-based write or atomic rename pattern in T4's lane-scheduler-spec.md'. However, lane-scheduler-spec.md line 70 explicitly states macOS has no flock(1) and exclusively uses mkdir-based locking. The ADR references 'flock-based write' as a valid option but this is impossible on macOS (the target platform), creating an internal contradiction between the ADR and the spec it cites. A developer reading the ADR would believe flock is an option when it isn't.
findings.fix_sketch: In ADR-004 Consequences, replace 'flock-based write or atomic rename pattern' with 'mkdir-based locking (as used in lane-lock.sh — macOS has no flock(1))'. This makes the ADR consistent with lane-scheduler-spec.md line 70 and self-heal-pipeline.md's corrected guidance.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md references regressions via index.json filter but section 2 input table still lists a separate regressions source path
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 2 input table (line 29) lists 'Audit regressions' with source path '<repo>/.audits/index.json filtered for status == "regression"'. This correctly describes the data model (no regressions.json exists). However, the description column says 'Bump priority on repeat bugs' which sounds like a separate REGRESSION-status concern, while the input just before it (line 28) already includes 'Audit findings (watch-list)' reading the same index.json. The Proposer spec describes reading index.json twice for the same file — once for all findings and once filtered for regression status — with no explanation of deduplication or processing order. An implementer would query the file twice or not understand this is a filter of the same dataset.
findings.fix_sketch: Clarify section 2 that 'Audit regressions' is NOT a separate file read but a filter pass over the already-loaded index.json findings array (status == 'regression'). Merge the two rows or add a note: 'loaded in same pass as audit findings above; regressions get +30 score bonus per section 3 ranking algorithm.'

findings.title: ADR-003 status enum lists 'reopened' but self-heal-pipeline and rubric never define it; trace event schema references it creating dead schema
findings.detail: ADR-003 (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 122) defines a finding status field with values 'open/fixing/verifying/closed/regression'. The rubric.json categories and self-heal-pipeline.md's data model do not include 'reopened' as a status (per the prior scan's finding AUDIT-audit-elevation-629286f0 which was correctly closed). However, ADR-003 also defines the new 'audit.finding.regressed' trace event kind (line 135) using payload shape `{ findingId, originalClosePr, regressionFingerprint, newOccurrenceTaskId }` — but this payload omits the `regression_of` and `regression_closing_pr` fields that self-heal-pipeline.md line 122-124 defines as required fields for regression findings in the scan JSON. The trace event and the scan file have diverging schemas for regression data, meaning the 'bidirectional' sync described in ADR-003 cannot work without data loss.
findings.fix_sketch: Align the audit.finding.regressed trace event payload with the scan-level regression fields. Add `regression_of` and `regression_closing_pr` to the trace event payload in ADR-003 line 135. Alternatively, add a note that these fields are folded into `newOccurrenceTaskId` — but make it explicit, not implicit.

findings.title: closed.json schema version field conflicts: top-level 'version' clashes with finding schema 'schema_version' convention
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md defines closed.json with a top-level 'version' field (integer, currently 1). rubric.json uses 'schema_version' (integer) and 'rubric_version' (string semver). The finding scan files use neither — they have no schema version field at all. Three related schemas in the same system use three different version field conventions ('version', 'schema_version', 'rubric_version'). The fingerprint_algo section of rubric.json also carries its own 'version' key ('sha256-v1' string). When the fingerprint algorithm changes and requires a schema bump, there is no clear guidance on which version field to bump in closed.json vs rubric.json, creating an operational confusion risk during migration.
findings.fix_sketch: Standardize on 'schema_version' (integer) across all system data files (closed.json, index.json, scan files). Document in rubric.json or a separate schema-versions.md that 'rubric_version' is for the rubric document itself while 'schema_version' tracks the data format. The fingerprint_algo 'version' string is fine as-is since it is the algorithm identifier, not a data-format version.

findings.title: Lane scheduler spec references lane-scheduler.pm2.json but ADR-004 describes ~lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs} with a now-removed .sh — spec/ADR conflict persists
findings.detail: ADR-004 line 164 refers to '~/.claude/scripts/lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs} (T4 ships tonight)' — this brace expansion implies a .sh file exists. The prior scan (AUDIT-audit-elevation-14de88a1) correctly identified that lane-scheduler.sh does not exist and closed the README finding. However, ADR-004 still carries the phantom .sh reference. The README was fixed but the ADR was not updated. A developer reading ADR-004 to understand fold-in scope would believe there are two scheduler scripts to wire into IFleet when there is only one (.mjs).
findings.fix_sketch: In ADR-004 Context section (line 164), change 'lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs}' to 'lane-scheduler.mjs'. This brings the ADR into sync with the README fix already applied and with actual disk contents.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md Budget gate logic is inverted: ENABLED flag absent means run, present means send — opposite of standard gating convention
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 7 (line 106) states: 'a flag file ~/.omc/proposer/ENABLED. If absent → Proposer runs (computes a proposal, writes state) but does NOT send to Discord.' This is semantically correct (absent = withheld, present = send). However, the phrasing 'If absent → Proposer runs' is actively misleading because 'runs' normally implies full execution including side effects. The actual behavior when ENABLED is absent is that the proposer computes but silently withholds the Discord send. Any developer implementing this would likely interpret 'runs' as 'sends' and implement the gate backwards, causing the Proposer to spam Discord from day one. The Failure modes table (line 100) also says 'Generate the proposal but do NOT send. Write to state file with WITHHELD_BY_BUDGET_GATE' but this is listed under 'Budget gate not lifted' as if the gate not being lifted is an error condition rather than the intended default.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the Budget gate description to: 'If ENABLED flag file is absent (default on install): compute proposal and write to state, but DO NOT send to Discord. If ENABLED flag file is present: compute and send.' Add an explicit note that absent=withheld is the INTENTIONAL default, not an error. Rename the failure mode row from 'Budget gate not lifted' to 'Budget gate closed (normal default state)' to prevent confusion.

findings.title: lane-scheduler-spec.md describes lane-list.sh color codes but NO_COLOR handling is documented as honored without specifying what 'honors' means
findings.detail: lane-scheduler-spec.md line 77 documents lane-list.sh as: 'Color codes: green OK, yellow STALE ... Honors NO_COLOR/non-TTY.' The phrase 'honors' is ambiguous — it could mean 'outputs no ANSI codes when NO_COLOR is set' (correct) or 'suppresses the status text entirely' (incorrect). The NO_COLOR spec (no-color.org) requires stripping color codes but keeping text. Without explicit statement that the text (OK/STALE/NO-HB) is preserved when colors are stripped, an implementer might suppress both color and status text in non-TTY mode, making the script output useless in CI/cron.
findings.fix_sketch: Change 'Honors NO_COLOR/non-TTY' to 'Strips ANSI color codes when NO_COLOR env var is set or stdout is not a TTY; status text (OK/STALE/NO-HB) is always emitted regardless of color mode.'

findings.title: quota-pacing-design.md references claude-opus-4-7 and claude-haiku-4-5 model IDs that may be stale naming conventions
findings.detail: quota-pacing-design.md section 3.1 weight table lists model IDs 'claude-opus-4-7', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5'. These appear to use a non-standard naming convention (4-7 instead of the common opus-4 or similar). The lane-scheduler-spec.md line 51 also uses 'claude-opus-4-7' as an example. While these are consistent within the codebase, if actual Anthropic model IDs differ (e.g., claude-opus-4), the weight lookup in the scheduler would fail to match real model IDs and fall through to the 'unknown' weight (2), incorrectly costing all Opus lanes as 'unknown'. This is low-risk now (design doc only) but will bite during Phase 4 implementation.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a note in quota-pacing-design.md section 3.1 that model IDs used in the weight table must match exactly what the claude CLI/API returns in model identifiers, and that the implementation should do a prefix match (e.g., startsWith('claude-opus')) rather than exact match to handle minor version suffixes gracefully.

findings.title: plan.md Phase 2 prerequisites section omits that Codex CLI install is a Sebastian-owned blocking task, buried in prose
findings.detail: plan.md section Phase 2 (line 107) states prerequisites Sebastian owns but formats them as a bullet list in the middle of a prose paragraph. The plan's critical files table (line 178) correctly structures the file work, but there is no equivalent tracking structure for non-file prerequisites (Codex CLI install, flat-rate subscription confirmation). The README Phase 2 status row correctly notes 'Codex CLI not installed' but plan.md has no corresponding gate or status indicator. Since plan.md is the 'original strategy plan that drove the build' (per README docs table), its prerequisites section should be as prominent as its file changes table.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a 'Blocked prerequisites (Sebastian owns)' table to Phase 2 in plan.md, separate from the files table, listing: 'Install Codex CLI (codex --version must resolve) — BLOCKING', 'Confirm flat-rate subscription active — BLOCKING'. Mark their current status. This mirrors the same structure used in the files table and makes the blocking dependency visible without digging into prose.
